questions.q: Open-chain glucose is treated with excess periodic acid. The products are:
questions.explain: Five C–C bonds are cut: C-1 (CHO) and C-2 to C-5 (CHOH) give formic acid and the terminal CH₂OH gives formaldehyde. The 3 HCOOH + 2 HCHO + CO₂ set belongs to fructose.

questions.q: Which compound is NOT cleaved by HIO₄?
questions.explain: Cleavage needs two neighbouring carbons that each carry O or N. In propane-1,3-diol the OH groups are separated by a CH₂, so no cyclic periodate ester forms.

questions.q: Which product is formed when open-chain fructose is cleaved by HIO₄ but NOT when glucose is?
questions.explain: The ketone carbon C-2 of fructose is cut on both sides and leaves as CO₂. Both sugars give HCOOH, HCHO and HIO₃.

questions.q: Glycerol, HOCH₂–CH(OH)–CH₂OH, is oxidised with excess HIO₄. The moles of HIO₄ consumed and the products per mole are:
questions.explain: Two C–C bonds join O-bearing carbons, so 2 HIO₄ are used. The two terminal CH₂OH carbons become HCHO and the inner CHOH, cut on both sides, becomes HCOOH.
